evidence:
The paragraph in cyclic.tex cites nothing. Three sources support it; Nanda does not.

1. Gromov 2023, arXiv 2301.02679, Sec. 3.1. I read the PDF text directly.
   - Eq. (10): the squared activation expands to include "+ cos(2pi k(n-m)/p + phi1 - phi2)".
   - Eq. (11): the second-layer preactivation includes cos(2pi k(n-m-q)/p + ...) and cos(2pi k(n-m+q)/p + ...). These are exactly the paper's beta_{j,T} copies.
   - Eq. (12): phi1 + phi2 = phi3 gives constructive interference.
   - Eqs. (14)-(15): "we need to ensure that all other waves (i.e. all terms, but the third term in (11)) interfere destructively". Random phases achieve this, since sum_k cos(2pi k s/p + phi_k) << N.
   - The cancellation is approximate. Our condition is exact (Def. if), and our per-neuron sign rule is new.

2. Morwani et al. ICLR 2024, arXiv 2311.07568 (HTML read).
   - App. F.3: a neuron's DFT is nonzero only if j = 0, k = 0, or "j,k,l = ±zeta". That set includes the mixed-sign, label-independent modes.
   - A max-margin f has f_hat supported only on j = k = -l (plus l = 0).
   - App. F.2 builds 8 neurons per frequency with paired phases, so the sum is exactly cos(a+b-c) and the rest cancels. This is an implicit interference-free construction; they never name the a-b term.

3. He, Wang, Chen, Yang, arXiv 2602.16849 (Feb 2026), Sec. 4.
   - Eq. (4.1): a quadratic neuron outputs the signal times cos(omega(x-y)/2)^2, plus "residual noise".
   - Def. 4.1 (full diversification, phase sums exp(i·iota·sum phi_m) = 0) and Prop. 4.2: the diversified neurons collectively cancel that noise.

4. Nanda et al. 2023 (PDF text grepped): discusses constructive and destructive interference of the logit cosines only. There is no a-b product-to-sum term, so do not cite it here.

Queries and sources used: arxiv.org/html/2301.02679, arxiv.org/pdf/2301.02679, arxiv.org/html/2311.07568v2, arxiv.org/pdf/2301.05217, arxiv.org/html/2602.16849.

recommended_citations.why: Supports the sentence on sign-flipped copies. Eqs. (10)-(11) explicitly contain cos(2pi k(n-m)/p) and cos(2pi k(n-m±q)/p). Eqs. (14)-(15) cancel them only approximately, through random phases across the width. Already in refs.bib.

App. F.3: a single neuron's DFT is nonzero at all sign patterns (j,k,l = ±zeta), while the max-margin f is supported only on j = k = -l. App. F.2 is an 8-neurons-per-frequency construction whose extra terms cancel exactly. This is an implicit interference-free max-margin network. Already in refs.bib.

Sec. 4, Eq. (4.1): quadratic-neuron product-to-sum output = signal times cos(omega(x-y)/2)^2 plus residual noise. Def. 4.1 (full diversification) and Prop. 4.2: phase-diversified neurons cancel that noise. Supports 'several neurons must cancel each other's copies'.

recommended_change: In cyclic.tex, after "...interference at the feature's own frequency.", add: "These copies appear explicitly in the analytic solutions of \citet{gromov2023grokking} (Eqs. 10--11), which cancel them only approximately, through random phases. They are implicit in the exact max-margin construction of \citet{morwani2024feature} (App. F.2--F.3) and in the phase-diversification condition of \citet{he2026mechanism} (Def. 4.1)." Add the he2026mechanism bib entry. Do not cite Nanda et al. 2023 for this point: it does not discuss the a-b term.
